method: Static first reasoned review: atomscan reports, cleave facts including decoded text, and rizin control-flow disassembly. Samples were not executed. Collector names, ML scores and prior review documents were not used to establish behavior.

samples.identification: VS Code concealed font-path launcher matching the GhostAction report
evidence: The single shell task passes ./public/fonts/fa-solid-400.woff2 as the Node program entry, rather than as data consumed by a font tool.
The same task declares folderOpen activation, hide=true, reveal=never, echo=false and close=true, under a lint-like label. These fields conceal a disguised program invocation.
The JSON task exactly matches the launcher reproduced in the linked primary report.
limits: The task requires appropriate VS Code task placement, workspace trust and automatic-task authorization, Node, and the companion file. The collected JSON is not independently executable.
The companion payload is absent. No credential access, exfiltration, cron persistence or other payload behavior is attributed to this JSON.
samples.marker_line: GhostAction VS Code launcher: clarify task path evidence

samples.identification: Damaged StormAttack x86 service/Active Setup DLL-injection loader
evidence: CRT entry 0x402674 calls dispatcher 0x401cb0. Mode dword at 0x404120 is 3. The mode-3 branch calls Active Setup helper 0x401900 and jumps to the appended .htext trampoline at 0x40f000, which calls self-delete helper 0x401390.

0x401900 creates a GUID-named HKLM Active Setup Installed Components subkey and writes an expandable StubPath at 0x401a4b. It reads its own file using CRT I/O, patches a copy, writes it with fwrite and invokes CreateProcessA.

The alternative mode-1 path extracts DLL resource 101 via 0x402460, writes it to a System32 DLL path, calls 0x401260 to replace LanmanServer Parameters/ServiceDLL, and calls 0x401150 to inject the DLL pathname into a child process.
The injector allocates and writes remote memory, resolves Kernel32!LoadLibraryA and passes the resolved function plus remote pathname to CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d.
Self-delete code obtains the module and short path, reads COMSPEC, appends /c del and > nul, and contains CreateProcessA/ResumeThread calls.
The .htext trampoline contains long canceling INC/DEC, self-move and self-exchange instruction runs, corroborating the existing junk-code traits.
limits: Several original instructions are damaged, portions of the IAT contain overwritten/bound values, and the embedded PE has zeroed code/import areas. Successful loading, injection, cleanup or persistence is not demonstrated.
Embedded HTTP and URLMon strings establish references only; the damaged resource is not evidence of working C2 or downloading.
The decoded-string fact is URL decoding of a percent-format GUID template. It is not an encoded URL or evidence of network contact.
No evidence of Remcos or WannaCry behavior was recovered.
changes: Removed Modify Registry (T1112) mappings from open/query/import-only observations and changed the co-occurrence description so it does not imply a dataflow chain. Matchers and notable criticality remain unchanged.
samples.marker_line: StormAttack damaged injector: correct registry-read mappings

samples.identification: Mirai-derived ARM Linux bot with remote device propagation
evidence: main at 0x132c8 initializes native attack vectors through 0x8614 and starts the scanner through 0x17560/0x159b8.

Scanner state code sends credentials and router shell-entry commands on remote sockets. At 0x166d8 it selects the BusyBox hostname marker; 0x16710 onward sends writable-directory tests and shell commands; 0x16838 selects chmod plus local payload execution. These buffers reach send wrapper 0x1a754.
The same state machine constructs BusyBox wget, TFTP, FTP and curl transfer/execute commands from fragments and sends them over the target session.

The main select loop calls 0x124c8. Its framed-receive helper 0x13c10 validates a 16-byte header/checksum and transforms payload bytes. Message type 3 sends the received buffer to attack parser 0x82bc.

The attack parser reads duration, vector, five-byte IPv4/netmask target records and key/value options; it invokes 0x81cc, which forks a timed child, selects an initialized vector and calls it indirectly.
Transport receive loop 0x13ff0..0x14024 and transmit loop 0x140f4..0x14124 apply XOR using four cyclic key bytes with evolving per-session positions.

0x12744 initializes a 256-byte RC4 state, schedules the eight-byte GET/dlr. key and unrolls four keystream XOR operations. Resolver 0x14830 calls it at 0x14d9c for selected four-byte DNS answer records. The token is not a payload-search comparison in this specimen.
limits: Network contact and successful infection were not tested. No decoded C2 answer or subsequent downloaded payload was available.
Literal API status and JSON/HTTP templates alone do not prove data theft or a command channel.
changes: Added code-based notable RC4 and direction-neutral cyclic-XOR observations.
Moved the two native-loader identities and their three token observations from the HTTP subtype to Mirai identity. Required matcher scopes and references were preserved.
Renamed dlr-payload-signature to compact-dlr-token. Plain family tokens and their co-occurrence are notable identity evidence, not suspicious behaviors.
samples.marker_line: Mirai ARM bot: add RC4/XOR traits and correct loader token claims

placement_and_reference_audit: Node dot-path matcher is unchanged and its sole exact YAML consumer was updated. A ./ prefix is a path entry, not evidence of a hidden filesystem object.

The five moved Mirai observations retain ELF/Linux gates, inherited size_max and all explicit sizes/confidences. There were no HTTP-only or identity-only directory-selector YAML consumers. Broad Mirai ancestors retain membership; exact/local references and current loader fixture expectations were updated.
The remaining beacon.yaml rules stay in the HTTP subtype. Historical review.json records are left as historical records.

Cyclic XOR belongs under data/codec because the same operation serves transmit and receive. The RC4 primitive fingerprint belongs in the existing RC4 leaf; neither new matcher infers malicious intent or an endpoint.

checks.code_controls: Both cyclic-XOR forms, ADD instead of XOR, wrong key cycle, no backward edge, non-code section and non-ARM. RC4 positive, missing state swap, missing output XOR, non-code section and non-ARM.
checks.loader_controls: Existing raw-error, ordinary GET, token-only and honest BusyBox updater fixtures must have zero hostile findings.
checks.rescans: All three atomscan rescans preserve existing findings after ID mapping. Only the ARM sample gains the two new code-based notable observations. No hostile coverage is removed.
